did_you_know.text: Did you know? Rehoboam gathered 180,000 warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight against the kingdom of Israel and restore the kingdom to himself.

Did you know? The prophet Shemaiah commanded in the name of the Lord that they should not fight against their brothers, so Rehoboam and the people obeyed and turned back from the war against Jeroboam.
Did you know? After the war was called off, Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and fortified cities in Judah, including Bethlehem, Tekoa, Lachish, Hebron, and Azekah.
Did you know? Rehoboam strengthened the fortified cities, appointed commanders over them, and stored food, olive oil, and wine in them.
Did you know? In each of the fortified cities, Rehoboam placed shields and spears, thereby greatly strengthening Judah and Benjamin militarily.
Did you know? The Levites left their pasturelands and possessions in the kingdom of Israel and moved to Judah and Jerusalem because Jeroboam and his sons had excluded them from serving as priests.

Did you know? According to the chapter, Jeroboam appointed priests for the high places, the goat demons, and the calves he had made, in contrast to the service of the priests and Levites in Jerusalem.
Did you know? People from all the tribes of Israel who wanted to worship the Lord, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices there to the Lord, the God of their ancestors.
Did you know? For three years, the kingdom of Judah and Rehoboam grew stronger because the people followed the way of David and Solomon.

Did you know? Rehoboam had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, who bore him twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters; he loved Maacah, the daughter of Absalom, more than all his other wives and concubines.
